entry.dc:title: EVALUATION OF FLORIDA PHOSPHATE MATRIX TRANSPORTATION FROM MINE TO PLANT.
entry.dc:creator: Raulerson J.
entry.dc:description: This paper presents a comparative evaluation of several systems currently being used or proposed for the transport of matrix from an open-pit mine to a large fixed plant. The matrix is a sticky, wet clay to be carried from 8-16 km (5-10 miles) at 910 t/h to 1. 8 kt/h (1,000-2,000 stph). The system is complicated by frequent moves of the open-pit mine site and other factors such as use of the clay component in land reclamation.

entry.dc:title: Torony Lignite Deposit - A Model for Development.
entry.dc:creator: Simon K.
entry.dc:description: The exploration of Pliocene lignite deposits in western Hungary began in the Koszeg-Szombathely-Szentgotthard area in 1962. Prospecting work ending in 1977 indicated the presence of considerable reserves. Extensive exploration work carried out after the initial development phase confirmed the presence of about 500 million tons of lignite reserves west of Szombathely up to the Austrian border. The coal seams continue westward into south Burgenland, but in the opinion of the author this part of the deposit is not large enough for the opening of a separate open-pit mine.

entry.dc:title: PRELIMINARY ANALYSIS OF THE MINOR STRUCTURES IN THE BAIYIN OPEN-PIT MINE, GANSU.
entry.dc:creator: Duan J.
entry.prism:publicationName: Zhongnan Kuangye Xueyuan Xuebao Journal of Central South Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: There are various types of minor structures occurring in the Baiyin Open-pit Mine, Gansu. On the basis of the deformation succession of the structures, it may be subdivided into two main phases and three subordinate stages, and all of them belong to the Caledonian Cycle. For all the stages, the styles of structure, dynamic characteristics, heat-flow values, strain-facies and metamorphism that have been found in the minor structures reveal certain regularities.

entry.dc:title: COSTS OF IN-PIT CRUSHING.
entry.dc:creator: Iles C.D.
entry.dc:description: Duval Corp. has historically been sensitive to mining costs, in part because of relatively low grade copper-molybdenum ore bodies. These concerns have resulted in three haulage system generations at the 218 kt/d (240,000 stpd) Sierrita-Esperanza open-pit mine, Tucson, Ariz. Studies indicate an average haulage cost savings of 32 cents/t(29 cents/st) of rock processed through the portable system. With three portable crushing systems handling 55% of the material mined, the total annual non-capital cash flow (before taxes) will increase more than 12 million. In addition, average truck requirements will be reduced by 37%, eliminating all truck capital expenditures over the next 10-year period.

entry.dc:title: NEW INDUSTRIAL TRACTION SETS.
entry.dc:creator: Dubina I.
entry.dc:description: Basic technical data are reported and structural features indicated for the new type OPE1B alternating-current and PEZT direct-current traction sets; they permit a 20-25% increase in the productivity of open-pit mine transportation in movement of material, with a substantial reduction in electric-power consumed for traction and expanded sphere of effective utilization of rail transport in deep open-pit mines.

entry.dc:title: DEVELOPING AND EVALUATING PIT TRUCK SAFETY DEVICES.
entry.dc:creator: Yates W.
entry.dc:description: Driver visibility is restricted in large, rear-dump haulage trucks used in open-pit mining. Analysis shows the need for an alarm to warn of vehicles in blind spots. Anaconda developed an electromagnetic system whereby smaller vehicles transmit a signal to haulage truck operators to alert them to their presence. The system has been field-tested at the Twin Buttes open-pit mine near Tucson, Ariz.

entry.dc:title: OPEN-PIT MINE PLANNING - THE EXPANDED ROLE OF COMPUTERS.
entry.dc:creator: Weiss A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: Applications of computer assisted mine planning are described in mineral exploration, development and operations. The strength of this tool lies in the improved ability to plan and execute mining projects. Such benefit is illustrated by three cases representing feasibility studies, long- to short-range mine planning, and operations monitoring and control. Quantitative benefit and cost data are presented.

entry.dc:title: EFFECT OF SHEARING ON THE QUALITY OF SOME COALS IN THE SOUTHEASTERN CANADIAN CORDILLERA.
entry.dc:creator: Bustin R.
entry.dc:description: Extensive deposits of tectonically sheared coal of the Mist Mountain Formation occur in the southeastern Canadian Cordillera. In order to determine the effect of shearing and comminution on washability, samples of sheared and unsheared coal of two seams were collected from an open-pit mine at Eagle Mountain. The results of investigation indicate that the sheared, finely comminuted coal has a disproportionately large amount of dash, lower yields on washing and is more extensively oxidized than the unsheared coal.

entry.dc:title: Development and recultivation of the Altenburg 4 lignite open-pit mine of the Preussische Elektrizitats-AG, Borken section
entry.dc:creator: Schroder H.

entry.dc:title: Numerical Simulation of Potentiometric Surface Changes Caused by a Proposed Open‐Pit Anthracite Mine
entry.dc:creator: Bair E.
entry.dc:description: The Trescott, Pinder, Larson (Trescott and others, 1976) finite‐difference flow model was modified and used to simulate potentiometric surface changes caused by the development of a proposed open‐pit anthracite mine. The modifications to the program code were made to account for site‐specific hydrogeologic conditions and to simulate the mining operation. In order to account for vertical changes in hydraulic conductivity caused by underground mine voids, the coefficient subroutine (COEF) was modified to permit the value of hydraulic conductivity to vary with depth. The lateral growth and deepening of the mine were simulated by changing the data input subroutine (DATAI) to allow the number, location, and hydraulic head of constant‐head nodes to vary with the time period. The mass balance subroutine (CHECKI) was modified to print out the flux into each constant‐head node at the end of each time period, thereby permitting calculation of changes in the rate of ground‐water flow into the mine. Site‐specific values of hydraulic conductivity, specific yield, aquifer recharge, streambed permeability, and hydraulic head initially were used in the modeling studies. Input parameter values were adjusted within the range of established field values during steady‐state model calibration. It was not possible to calibrate the transient model because the mining operation was in the planning stage and, therefore, no historical data existed. Nonetheless, transient simulations using the adjusted input parameter values and the simulated hydraulic head values were made to show that it is possible to model potentiometric surface changes caused by ground‐water flow into an open‐pit mine. These simulations predicted that, after eight years of mining, a cone of depression approximately 20,000‐feet long, 8000‐feet wide, and 1000‐feet deep would form around the proposed mine. The results of the transient simulations were used in a preliminary manner to assess the potential hydrogeologic impact of the proposed mining operation. Copyright © 1981, Wiley Blackwell. entry.dc:title: ESTIMATING DRILLING AND BLASTING COSTS - AN ANALYSIS AND PREDICTION MODEL.
entry.dc:creator: Borquez G.
entry.dc:description: Drilling and blasting cost estimates that closely approximate eventual operating costs are important to mining companies and their contractors. Mining companies need accurate estimates to evaluate financially ongoing projects and assess bids from contractors. The key to accurate cost estimates lies in identifying and accounting for all of the factors that affect the financing of a particular operation. In this paper, an analysis of the drilling, blasting, operating, and economic parameters that should be accounted for in a drilling and blasting program are identified and treated quantitatively. The parameters are then used to help design a cost estimate for driling and blasting in the preproduction program of a large open-pit mine.

entry.dc:title: SHORT-DELAY BLASTING AT ANACONDA'S BERKELEY OPEN-PIT MINE, MONTANA.
entry.dc:creator: Oriard L.L.
entry.dc:description: The authors outline the development and application of blasting methods put into use 11 years ago. The blast design uses a very short delay (5 milliseconds) between detonation of explosives charges. Concern is expressed over categorical rejection of very short delay blasting which can make the difference between success and failure of major mining operations.

entry.dc:title: KAISER JOINS THE BIG COAL PRODUCERS.
entry.dc:creator: Jackson D.
entry.dc:description: Kaiser Resources Ltd. is preparing to install a new generation of equipment at its Sparwood mine in British Columbia. KRL has broken ground for the Green Hills open-pit mine.

entry.dc:title: Pneumatic piezometers: multiple and single installations in vertical and inclined boreholes.
entry.dc:creator: Deardorff G.
entry.dc:description: A large-scale slope optimization program was undertaken in the Twin Buttes open-pit mine in Arizona, USA. A key element of this program was the depressurization of a fault zone, which intersects the pit wall. In order to monitor the effectiveness of the depressurization program and to establish water pressure gradients within the fault zone affected by surface and underground mining and drilling, multiple installations of up to three sealed pneumatic piezometers in one borehole were installed to depths in excess of 274m. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: CYPRUS BAGDAD.
entry.dc:creator: Niemi L.
entry.dc:description: Details are given of Cyprus Bagdad Copper Co. 's major expansion in northwestern Arizona, which was designed to increase the company's annual copper production from approximately 35 million lbs to more than 140 million lbs. The open-pit mine and 40,000-stpd concentrator, located 120 miles northwest of Phoenix in the Santa Maria Mtns. at Bagdad, now accounts for over 7% of Arizona's copper output and 4. 5% of US production. The ″new″ Cyprus Bagdad is an excellent example of a safe, clean, and highly efficient operation which reflects the successful application of ″state-of-the-art″ mining and processing techniques.

entry.dc:title: 7 DAYS TO MINE EIGHT SEAMS.
entry.dc:creator: Jackson D.
entry.dc:description: This article describes how the financial advantages of a seven-day, three-shift operation were used by Carbon Coal Co. to maximize the mining of eight thin, elusive coal seams at the company's New Mexico open-pit mine. Mining the multiple seams at the Mentmore, N. M. , mine required elaborate and crucial scheduling at times. The flow chart of the mine's coal preparation plant is included.

entry.dc:title: Opening of the Hambach Open-Pit Brown Coal Mine and the Mine Infrastructure.
entry.dc:creator: Berkenbusch J.
entry.dc:description: The coal field has extractable coal deposits of 2400 million tons. With an annual output of 45 to 50 million tons, the Hambach open-pit mine will provide about 40% of the total output of the Rhine Brown Coal Company until far beyond the year 2000. After the definition of responsibilities had been announced in May 1977, it was essential to equip the new open-pit mine with the required construction plant for the infrastructure. In this respect three aspects can be distinguished - namely, 1. the conveyor plant for the transport of water, waste and coal away from the coalfield; 2. the plant for opening up the area to traffic; and the 3. plant for surface construction work at the extraction base and dumping base.

entry.dc:title: MINIMIZING FAILURES OF TRUCK HOIST CYLINDERS AND FRAMES.
entry.dc:creator: Blaylock J.
entry.dc:description: Normally, the hydraulic system and structures are considered to be unrelated items. In reality, the two cannot be separated because one affects and depends on the other to function properly. This paper explores the potential failure areas of hydraulic cylinders, such as used on open-pit mine trucks, and suggests possible methods to prevent failures from occurring. The use of high-strength low-alloy steel in frames is reviewed and the benefits discussed.

entry.dc:title: COMPUTER APPLICATIONS IN OPEN-PIT MINE PLANNING.
entry.dc:creator: Garg O.
entry.dc:description: This paper summarizes the computer applications in open-pit mine planning at the Iron Ore Company of Canada (IOC). A brief history of the use of computers at IOC is given, and a description of the existing facilities is outlined. The following systems are discussed: storage and retrieval of geological data; geotechnical data analysis; long-term grade and tonnage forecasting; ore grading; and open-pit mine design. Justification for using computers in open-pit mine planning is given, and possible future areas of application are considered.

entry.dc:title: AMERICAN NUCLEAR IS BROADENING ITS HORIZONS.
entry.dc:creator: White L.
entry.dc:description: A brief outline is given of the expanding activities of American Nuclear Corp. in uranium drilling mining and milling. Currently one of the smaller companies participating in U. S. uranium development, American Nuclear is mapping out plans to quadruple feed capacity at its Gas Hill mill, from 1,000 stpd to 4,000 stpd, and is also developing its new Cotter Ferguson open-pit mine in the Gas Hills. In the northern Powder River Basin, the company is conducting detailed drilling on properties held jointly with TVA to define reserves that may become the basis of a mine-mill complex, with startup possible in 1984. Further, seismic techniques are being used to identify channels of possible uranium deposition under the Sweetwater Plateau south of the Gas Hills.

entry.dc:title: TREND TOWARDS MECHANICAL DRIVES FOR OPEN-PIT MINE HAULAGE TRUCKS.
entry.dc:creator: Williams R.
entry.dc:description: There has been a trend to the mechanical drive concept in the 85-ton class truck during the past few years. It appears that this trend is continuing throughout the range of mid-size end dump trucks, up to and including 120-ton units.

entry.dc:title: Impressions of the Chinese Mining Industry.
entry.dc:creator: Fettweis G.
entry.dc:description: The author gives his impressions, obtained during a visit to the Chinese People's Republic from Oct. 21 to Nov. 4, 1977, of mining operations in the northern, northeastern, and southern parts of China, with particular attention paid to coal mining. After briefly noting the estimated coal reserves in China, the organization of the mining industry, the degree of modernization, and estimated output, the author discusses the damage caused by the earthquakes of 1976 and reviews the mining techniques currently used, most of the coal mines being undergound mines worked by longwall retreating. Finally, the author describes his visits to two underground coal mines and one open-pit mine.

entry.dc:title: Development of Scheelite Mining at Mittersill.
entry.dc:creator: Spross W.
entry.prism:publicationName: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: A short historical review of the discovery, exploration and development of the scheelite deposit in the Felbertal near Mittersill, Austria, is presented. Details are given of the open-pit mine planning, ore extraction, and stripping operations. The development of the deposit's western part for underground mining is also covered, and some aspects of the ore dressing operations are outlined.

entry.dc:title: GEOLOGY OF THE CARGILL PHOSPHATE DEPOSIT IN NORTHERN ONTARIO.
entry.dc:creator: Sandvik P.
entry.dc:description: The Cargill phosphate deposit, located 32km. southwest of Kapuskasing, was discovered in 1975 and has been evaluated through an extensive program of 190 drill holes, numerous chemical analyses, metallurgical tests, and engineering and economic studies. The alkalic complex, comprising principally carbonatite and pyroxenite-amphibolite rocks, has been interpreted to have been intruded into the rift system of the Kapuskasing High during late Precambrian near the intersection of northeast- and northwest-trending faults. The complex is one of at least ten known alkalic complexes in or close to the magnetic-gravity-high system and is expressed by an elongated, northeast-oriented, three-part magnetic anomaly 7. 2km. long by 2. 3km. wide. Vermiculite, columbium-bearing minerals, clay minerals and quartz sand are present in quantities that suggest the possibility of commercial development. Uranium is absent or occurs only in very minor amounts. A tentative open-pit mine, designed for preliminary feasibility studies, is estimated to contain a probable phosphate-bearing deposit of 62. 5 million metric tons at an average grade of 19. 6 per cent P//2O//5.

entry.dc:title: Mechanism of Deformation of Rocky and Semirocky Banks.
entry.dc:creator: Turintsev Y.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: Based on natural and laboratory investigations, a hypothesis is worked out about the mechanism of deformation of rocky and semirocky open-pit mine slopes in pre-limit and limit equilibrium stages. The proposed hypothesis permits prediction of the character of development of the deformation of banks. This is necessary for timely and correct elaboration of measures to prevent such deformations.
